historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah, Volume 11, page 307. The Islamic conquests of Persia and the establishment of the Rashidun Caliphate under Caliph Umar ibn Al-Khattab (632-644 AD). Nikrouz was a prominent Persian scholar and a vizier of the last Sassanid king Yazdigird III (632-651 AD). He played a significant role in the negotiations between Yazdigird and Umar, but ultimately failed to prevent the Islamic conquest of Persia.
historical_references.context: Negotiations between the last Sassanid king and the Rashidun Caliphate regarding Islamic conquest of Persia

historical_references.reference: Al-Masudi's Muruj al-Dhahab, Volume 1, page 277. The Umayyad Caliphate (661-750 AD) and the establishment of Arab rule in Persia. Nikrouz became the governor of Fars province after serving as a vizier under the Sassanid king. He was instrumental in the Arab conquest of Fars by facilitating the accommodation of the Arab forces and guiding them towards the capital city of Persepolis.
historical_references.context: Governor of Fars province during the Arab conquest of Persia under the Umayyad Caliphate
